fact_text: Supernet Limited was formed in 1995 and sells connectivity, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and renewable energy and power solutions to government, defence, telecom, enterprise and banking clients.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Supernet says it delivers connectivity to more than 11,000 bank branches alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Supernet's management said it has set up an entity in Dubai and is building a regional hub there, with partnerships under way with different satellite operators.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said subsea cable faults in Pakistan are frequent and prolonged compared with regional countries, which is why the impact is seen as larger than elsewhere.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Subsea cables wear and age, so their fault frequency is low when new and rises as the cable gets older.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Repair time for a subsea cable fault depends on the cable's position at sea, storms, and how far the repair ship must travel; the interviewee cited repair times of 4, 6 or 10 days.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said only a few cable repair ships exist, and they are busy both laying new cable and rectifying faults, which lengthens outages.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Pakistan's international connectivity depends mainly on two or three subsea cable systems, so when one is cut, capacity shifts to the remaining links and causes congestion and slow internet.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee argued Pakistan should diversify across many more subsea cables instead of two or three, and connect through landing stations in neighbours such as Oman and the UAE, where major cables terminate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Anchors dragged along the seabed can cut subsea cables, so the interviewee recommended routing a new cable at least 25 to 30 km from existing cables to lower the risk of a simultaneous cut.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Most of Pakistan's subsea cables come from the Middle East, a politically sensitive region, and a fault off Yemen took a long time to repair because of hostile activity in the area.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: According to the interviewee, Afghanistan's total internet traffic depends on Pakistan, and Central Asian routes to the outside world run through Afghanistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Pakistan has a terrestrial internet link to China, but the interviewee noted that China runs a separate internet, which local firms see as a limit on its relevance to Pakistani users.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee expected that resolving Pakistan's issues with Iran would open a terrestrial route through Iran toward Turkey and onward to Europe.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said the electricity corridor and the Turkmenistan pipeline projects did not materialise for several reasons, and that private investors are unlikely to commit money in such an uncertain area.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: A 2020 report cited by the interviewee found that only 2,800 of 15,000 websites with a .pk domain are hosted locally, so most Pakistani web content is hosted overseas.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said governments prefer to keep data inside their borders for security, and that data held abroad can be exposed to sanctions or disruption.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan lacks data centre services of the scale offered by Azure, Amazon or Google, and frequent outages reduce business confidence in local facilities.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said power is more expensive per unit in Pakistan than in the US, and backup systems add cost, so cloud hosting abroad is cheaper than local hosting.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: About 97% of Pakistan's cell towers are connected by fibre optic, while the rest rely on radio links that the interviewee described as less reliable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: A cell tower has a fixed capacity, so when many customers stream video at the same evening peak, speeds slow; the interviewee said cellular is serving homes that lack fibre.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said large-screen 4K video needs far more data than a small screen, so growing home fibre adoption will push data demand higher.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Right-of-way charges are levied by government or municipal bodies when roads are dug to lay underground cable and ducts; the government waived these charges, which the interviewee called a step in the right direction for fibre.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Pakistan has four provinces with many divisions and tehsils, and the interviewee said a uniform approval process across them would ease business and investment, since firms face different steps in each tehsil.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The government planned a 5G spectrum auction, which the video said was expected in March 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Similar claims of faster internet were made before the 2017 and 2021 spectrum auctions, but the interviewee said speed gains did not match those claims.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said the 5G auction should be investment-friendly, with a lower upfront spectrum price, so operators have a business case for 5G network, handset and local access-network investment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said 5G home routers could deliver fibre-like home service without new fibre to each home, while higher-capacity 5G sites would themselves need more fibre backhaul.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said average revenue per user in Pakistan is very low, which makes the investment case for telecom infrastructure difficult.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: Pakistan's personal data protection bill has been tabled for roughly two to three years and had not been approved as of Feb 2026, so personal data leaks go unchecked.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The government is working on setting up a national cybersecurity authority, with acts and regulations being drafted, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The State Bank of Pakistan sets cybersecurity policies and checks bank compliance, and in a cyber drill with the Pakistan Banking Association, 24 or 25 banks took part.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority has issued its own cybersecurity regulations and requires telecom operators to show compliance every year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The interviewee said each sector regulator acts on its own initiative, so a national cybersecurity authority is needed above them to unify responses to attacks on critical infrastructure.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The speaker said a country should be connected through at least 15 to 20 submarine cables so that one cut does not isolate its internet.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)

fact_text: The speaker estimated about 125 million cellular subscribers on 3G and 4G in Pakistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What’s Behind Pakistan’s Slow Internet and How to Fix It | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-02-12)
